bugs.name: Saving a user's repository limit as 0 resets it to -1
bugs.summary: The report says that in Site Administration > Edit User Account, saving Maximum Number of Repositories as 0 makes the form show -1 when reopened.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that a saved limit of 0 is shown as 0 when the form is reopened.
bugs.actual: After updating a user with a maximum repository count of 0, reopening the edit form was reported to show -1.
reproSteps: In Site Administration, edit a user account.
Set Maximum Number of Repositories to 0 and update the account.
Reopen the edit form and check the value.
bugs.reason: Not reproduced: saving 0 keeps 0. Across repeated attempts on a new user and a seeded user, typed and entered by keyboard, the request sent max_repo_creation=0 and the reopened form showed 0 every time; the server passes 0 through unchanged.

bugs.name: Monitoring Trace opens an empty diagnostic list
bugs.summary: The report claims that Site Administration > Monitoring > Trace shows only the Goroutines count header with a blank list below it, as if the diagnostic list failed to load.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects the Trace page to list goroutines or processes when it opens.
bugs.actual: Opening Trace from the sidebar showed '<N> Goroutines' with no list under it.
reproSteps: Sign in as a site administrator.
bugs.reason: Intended: routers/web/admin/stacktrace.go deliberately loads no process data until Running Processes or Stacktrace is chosen ('by default, do not do anything which might cause server errors… this page is the entrance of the chance to collect diagnosis report'), so the page stays usable for downloading a diagnosis report when the server is struggling. Both tabs load the list. That the page doesn't tell the administrator how to see traces is a separate accepted bug, gitea-admin-trace-page-hides-how-to-see-traces.

bugs.name: Diagnosis report ignores the 5-second minimum profiling duration
bugs.summary: The report says that the diagnosis report should profile for at least 5 seconds (range 5–300), but durations below 5 seconds are accepted and 0, empty or invalid values produce a report of about 1 second.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that durations of 5 seconds or less are raised to 5 seconds.
bugs.actual: seconds=0, empty and abc took about 1 second, seconds=3 took about 3 seconds, and seconds=10 took about 10 seconds.
reproSteps: Enter 0, 1 or 3 in the Download diagnosis report field and download.
bugs.reason: Intended: there is no 5-second minimum in this version. routers/web/admin/diagnosis.go clamps the duration to 1–300 seconds (if seconds <= 1 { seconds = 1 }); go-gitea/gitea#32973 ('Support performance trace', merged before v1.24) deliberately lowered the floor from 5 to 1, so the measured timings are the implemented behaviour. The accepted separate defect is that input below 1 second or non-numeric input is silently turned into a 1-second report with no message: 'Diagnosis report silently turns a duration below 1 second into a 1-second report'.

bugs.name: Admin repository delete link has no accessible name
bugs.summary: The report says the trash-icon delete link in Site Administration > Repositories is exposed to assistive technology as an unnamed link.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that the link has an accessible name such as Delete repository <name>.
bugs.actual: The anchor contains only an aria-hidden trash SVG with no text, title or aria-label; clicking it opens the Delete This Repository confirmation.
reproSteps: Sign in as an administrator and open /-/admin/repos.
Inspect the Op. cell's trash link in the accessibility tree.
bugs.reason: Out of scope: this is screen-reader accessibility (accessible name on an icon-only link), not a functional defect. The behaviour is as described (templates/admin/repo/list.tmpl renders the link with only {{svg "octicon-trash"}}), but the icon is visible and the link opens the delete confirmation. Accessibility findings are excluded from this benchmark's ground truth.

bugs.name: Admin configuration and user status icons have no text alternative
bugs.summary: The report says boolean values on Configuration Summary and the User Accounts Activated/Restricted/2FA columns are rendered only as aria-hidden check/cross SVGs, so screen readers announce empty values.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that each value exposes accessible text such as Yes/No.
bugs.actual: Each dd or table cell contains only an SVG with aria-hidden=true; Local Mode (check) and Disable Router Log (cross) are indistinguishable in the accessibility tree.
reproSteps: Sign in as an administrator and open /-/admin/config.
Inspect Local Mode and Disable Router Log values in the accessibility tree.
Open /-/admin/users and inspect the Activated, Restricted and 2FA cells.
bugs.reason: Out of scope: this is screen-reader accessibility (missing text alternatives), not a functional defect. The values are rendered as described (templates/admin/config.tmpl and templates/admin/user/list.tmpl use {{svg (Iif ... "octicon-check" "octicon-x")}}), but the check and cross icons are visible and correct. Accessibility findings are excluded from this benchmark's ground truth.
